beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:curious, inviting]Picture a town, more than two thousand years old, where nearly every house@noun had its own ^bathtub.
[d:tension][act:the mystery, quieter]Then, around {250|two fifty} BCE, everyone ^left. [act:hushed][tune:fall]And nobody ever came ^back.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]This is ^Kerkouane, on Cap ^Bon, a peninsula in northeast Tunisia, pointing out into the ^sea. [act:explaining]It was a ^Punic town: its people spoke the language of Carthage, their big ^neighbour. [act:storytelling]Spotted in {1952|nineteen fifty-two}, and a World Heritage site since {1985|nineteen eighty-five}.

[d:build][act:vivid, admiring][tune:level]A grid of ^streets, laid out to a plan, crossing at right angles like a modern ^city. [tune:level]A ^well in the courtyards. [act:the delightful detail][tune:fall]And baths with ^seats, lined in red ^mortar. [act:a simple picture, smiling]You sat ^in them, knees up, like a deep armchair of ^water.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:precise]Perhaps twelve hundred people lived here. [act:intrigued]They made purple ^dye from sea snails. [act:explaining]Each snail gives only a tiny ^drop, which made purple a ^luxury.

[d:build][act:gentle, curious]Set into the paving of one floor, a simple sign: the symbol of the goddess ^Tanit, a triangle, a bar, and a ^circle. [act:explaining]Tanit was one of the great goddesses of ^Carthage. [act:wonder]And from the tombs nearby, a rare painted wooden ^lid, nicknamed the Princess of ^Kerkouane.
[d:reveal][act:the turn, measured][tune:fall]So why ^leave? [act:weighing, careful]In {256|two fifty-six} BCE, a Roman army under ^Regulus landed on Cap Bon, right on this ^coast.

[d:build][act:the likely answer, calm]War is the likely ^reason. [p:0.93][act:an honest caveat]But notice how we know: the town ends just as the army ^arrives. [act:a simple picture]Two dates on the same page of a ^calendar: a strong hint, not a ^confession. [act:honest][tune:fall]The link comes from the ^timing, not from a written record@noun.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it][tune:rise]A Punic town, left around {250|two fifty} BCE and never ^rebuilt? [act:the verdict, confident][tune:fall]*Strong ^evidence*. [act:open, fair]Exactly ^why, is still debated.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:wistful]Carthage fell, and ^rose again. [act:the last word, quiet][tune:fall]Kerkouane just ^stopped. [act:quiet wonder, warm]Which is exactly why its streets ^survive.
